claim_verdicts.evidence: git show stage-1:DonHang.Api/Controllers/ProductsController.cs: `[Route("api/v1/products")] public sealed class ProductsController(DonHangDbContext db) : ControllerBase` with `[HttpGet] public async Task<ActionResult<List<ProductDto>>> List()` whose body is `var products = await db.Products.Select(p => new ProductDto(p.Id, p.Name, p.PriceVnd)).ToListAsync();`. Method name, route, expression and `db.Products` all match the claim character-for-character.

tools/extract-code DonHang.Api/Dtos.cs --tag stage-1 --lines 1-13 returns exactly the five records in the claim, in that order: ProductDto(int Id, string Name, int PriceVnd); OrderItemDto(int ProductId, int Quantity, int UnitPriceVnd); OrderDto(int Id, int CustomerId, string Status, DateTimeOffset PlacedAt, List<OrderItemDto> Items); CreateOrderItemRequest(int ProductId, int Quantity, int UnitPriceVnd); CreateOrderRequest(List<CreateOrderItemRequest> Items). All `public sealed record`.

DonHang.Domain/Entities.cs at stage-1: `public sealed class Product { public int Id { get; set; } public required string Name { get; set; } public int PriceVnd { get; set; } }` — exactly three properties, the same three ProductDto lists.

DonHang.Domain/Entities.cs: `public sealed class OrderItem { public int OrderId; public int ProductId; public int Quantity; public int UnitPriceVnd }` (all `{ get; set; }`). DonHang.Api/Dtos.cs: `OrderItemDto(int ProductId, int Quantity, int UnitPriceVnd)` — OrderId is the one property absent.

DonHang.Domain/Entities.cs: `public sealed class Customer` declares Id, `required string FullName`, `required string Email`, `required string City`, and `public string? PasswordHash { get; set; }` (comment: "Null until the customer sets a password; added by the AddPasswordHashToCustomers migration"). Nullable, so the lesson's "`null` or not" is possible.

refs/aspnetcore-docs web-api/advanced/formatting.md, moniker `>= aspnetcore-7.0` (covers 10.0): "use JsonOptions.JsonSerializerOptions. The following highlighted code configures PascalCase formatting instead of the default camelCase formatting". dotnet-docs system-text-json/configure-options.md, "Web defaults for JsonSerializerOptions": "PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase". The ledger's caveat also holds: how-to.md says STJ's own default is "casing of JSON names matches the .NET names". Program.cs calls AddControllers() with no JsonOptions override.

No Docker daemon here, so I could not curl the live lab. Recorded run at this tag, outputs/stage-1/scripts/backend/auth-and-orders.txt, line 2: `[{"id":1,"name":"Bàn phím cơ","priceVnd":1250000},...]` — the exact object, camelCase. db/seed.sql: `(1, 'Bàn phím cơ', 1250000)`. ProductsController.Get: `return Ok(new ProductDto(product.Id, product.Name, product.PriceVnd));` — same record, same serializer, so /products/1 emits that same object. Caddyfile `:8080 { handle /api/v1/* { reverse_proxy api:8080 } }` and compose publishes 8080, so the host URL is right.

dotnet-docs system-text-json/configure-options.md, "Web defaults for JsonSerializerOptions": "The following options have different defaults for web apps: PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true". character-casing.md repeats it: "The web default is case-insensitive." Note this claim is no longer asserted anywhere in the lesson text — section 4 now says only "What an incoming body's field names should look like is left for a later lesson" — so it is a ledger entry with no matching sentence, which is harmless.

dotnet-docs how-to.md, Serialization behavior: "By default, all public properties are serialized." ignore-properties.md: "To ignore all null-value properties, set DefaultIgnoreCondition to JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull" — i.e. nulls are written unless you opt out, and Program.cs sets no DefaultIgnoreCondition. With the web camelCase policy (claim 6), Customer.PasswordHash is written as `passwordHash`.

DonHang.Api/Controllers/OrdersController.cs: `[ApiController] [Route("api/v1/orders")]` with `[Authorize] [HttpPost] public async Task<ActionResult<OrderDto>> Create(CreateOrderRequest request)`. refs/aspnetcore-docs web-api/index.md, Binding source parameter inference: "[FromBody] is inferred for complex type parameters not registered in the DI Container." CreateOrderRequest is not in DI, so it binds from the body.

issues.quote: False, because `Product` is also used by code outside the API, so it cannot be reshaped as freely as a DTO can.
issues.text: Option d is marked wrong but is not actually wrong: at stage-1 `Product` lives in DonHang.Domain and is used outside the API by DonHangDbContext, EfOrderRepository and OrderService, so the statement is true of this codebase. The lesson also points that way — section 5 says Dtos.cs is "kept in one file separate from `DonHang.Domain`, the project that holds the server's internal types". Two same-polarity options (c and d) are both defensible rebuttals; the explanation for d concedes this by arguing only that the text never says it.
issues.fix: Replace option d with a genuinely false rebuttal, e.g. en: "False, because `Product` has four properties and `ProductDto` has three, so they cannot be merged" / vi: "Sai, vì `Product` có bốn property còn `ProductDto` có ba, nên không gộp được", and rewrite d's explanation to say both types list exactly Id, Name, PriceVnd today (Entities.cs and Dtos.cs at stage-1), so the premise is false — the real reason is the one in option c.

issues.quote: by default, each property name is written in camelCase for a response
issues.text: "by default" has no agent anywhere in the lesson (sections 3, 4, 6 and summary line 4 all state it bare). camelCase is the web-app default the API applies, not a property of JSON or of serialization in general; the .NET default without it is "casing of JSON names matches the .NET names" (dotnet-docs how-to.md). A reader who serializes a type outside an endpoint gets PascalCase and will think the lesson lied. The clause "for a response" is the only thing currently carrying the condition.
issues.fix: Give the default an owner once, in section 3's naming bullet, without new vocab: "— by default the server writes each property name in camelCase when it answers a request: ...". Leave the other three mentions as they are; they inherit the condition.

issues.quote: An `OrderItemDto` only ever appears inside an `OrderDto`, in the `Items` list above
issues.text: Unlisted claim: a statement about the whole codebase ("only ever") that q5's marked answer depends on, with no entry in .meta.json. I verified it — `git grep -n OrderItemDto stage-1` returns exactly three hits: the record in Dtos.cs, the `List<OrderItemDto> Items` member of OrderDto, and OrdersController.ToDto building that list — so it is true at this tag, but it is the kind of sentence that silently rots when the repo changes and the ledger is what makes it re-checkable.
issues.fix: Add to .meta.json claims: {"n": 11, "text": "At stage-1 OrderItemDto appears only as the element type of OrderDto.Items and in OrdersController.ToDto, never as a standalone response or request type.", "kind": "fact", "source_hint": "git grep OrderItemDto at tag stage-1", "needs_verification": true, "section": 5}. No change to the lesson text.

issues.quote: it walks the DTO's properties and writes one JSON field per property, with no further code from you
issues.text: Unlisted claim: a behaviour statement about the serializer (every property becomes a field, nothing else does) with no ledger entry — claim 6 covers only the name casing and claim 2 only the record declarations. It is true as written for these DTOs: dotnet-docs how-to.md, Serialization behavior, "By default, all public properties are serialized" and "By default, fields are ignored"; record.md: "A positional record class ... declare init-only properties", so each name in the parentheses really is a public property.
issues.fix: Add to .meta.json claims: {"n": 12, "text": "By default System.Text.Json serializes every public property of the returned type, one JSON field each, and ignores fields.", "kind": "behavior", "version_key": "aspnetcore", "source_hint": "dotnet-docs system-text-json/how-to.md, Serialization behavior", "needs_verification": true, "section": 4}. No change to the lesson text.

issues.quote: the last one `null`, since every customer tested so far signed up before Đơn Hàng had passwords
issues.text: The scenario's premise contradicts the stage-1 system it is set in: migration 20260923154700_AddPasswordHashToCustomers runs `UPDATE customers SET password_hash = '100000.O2f9...' WHERE id IN (1, 2, 3, 4, 5);`, so in the running lab all five seeded customers have a real hash — a student who tries `GET /api/v1/customers/{id}` reasoning would expect the hash, not null. The marked answer a stays correct either way; only the premise is false of this repo.
issues.fix: Replace the clause with one that does not claim anything about the seeded rows, e.g. en: "— the last one `null`, because the row they tested with was added by hand and never got a password" / vi: "— trường cuối là `null`, vì dòng dữ liệu họ dùng để thử được thêm tay và chưa từng đặt mật khẩu". Option a and its explanation need no change.

issues.text: The fill answer set has one spelling. The question says "a JSON field named ____", and the lesson and Try it both show the name inside quotes (`"priceVnd":1250000`), so a reader who types the quoted form is answering correctly and would be marked wrong. Not an ambiguity in the key — `priceVnd` is the right answer — only an incomplete accepted-spelling list.
issues.fix: Extend the answer array to ["priceVnd", "\"priceVnd\""] so the quoted JSON spelling is accepted too. Leave the explanation unchanged.

issues.quote: `ProductsController.List()`, from the last lesson, does exactly this: `new ProductDto(p.Id, p.Name, p.PriceVnd)`
issues.text: `ProductsController.List()` is handed to me as something I already saw, but what I was told about the last lesson is only that `GET /api/v1/products` answers with a JSON array — no class, no method. So I meet two names at once and have to take on faith that this is the code behind that endpoint. The mapping line itself is clear now that `p` is named; the owner of the line is not.
issues.fix: After "`ProductsController.List()`, from the last lesson", insert ", the method that answers `GET /api/v1/products`," so the name is tied to the endpoint I was told about.

issues.quote: A DTO can match its entity's fields today and still be worth keeping separate, since only the DTO is a promise to every client.
issues.text: Summary line 5 gives a reason no section gave me: that the DTO, and only it, is "a promise to every client". The reason the lesson argued was different — the entity may later hold a field a client must never see, or drop one a client depends on. Nothing in the body calls a DTO a promise, or says the entity is not one, so the last line I read introduces a new idea after the lesson has ended.
issues.fix: Rewrite the tail of summary line 5 with the reason the body gives, e.g. "...and still be worth keeping separate, because the entity can later gain a field no client should see."

issues.quote: Actually the default JSON options write every property name in camelCase for a response
issues.text: "The default JSON options" is a thing I have never met. Core concepts told me camelCase happens "because that is the default", which I accepted; "options" now suggests a named settings object somewhere that could be changed, which the lesson never shows. I understand the behaviour, but I stop to wonder what I am supposed to picture, and whether I missed it earlier.
issues.fix: Use the Core concepts wording in both places: section 6 -> "by default, each property name is written in camelCase for a response"; summary line 4 -> "By default, each property name is written in camelCase for a response".

issues.quote: This lesson only covers that direction; what an incoming request body's field names should look like is not something Try it below exercises.
issues.text: I read this pair of sentences twice. The first half is about what the lesson covers, the second about what the exercise does, and the closing "Nothing in `ProductDto` asks for this, and nothing in this lesson changes it" points "this" and "it" back at camelCase two sentences earlier. I finished the paragraph unsure whether incoming field names are camelCase too or simply not discussed.

issues.quote: What could go wrong later, once `Product` needs to hold something a client should never see, that this response gives no hint of right now?
issues.text: I can picture the teammate and the shortcut, and the lesson does answer the question. But the question runs long and its final clause, "that this response gives no hint of right now", sits far from what it modifies — I first attached it to `Product`, re-read, then attached it to the thing that could go wrong.
issues.fix: Split it in two: "Today's response gives no hint of it. What goes wrong later, once `Product` has to hold something a client should never see?"
